newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends down on BOJ rate concern report.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends down on BOJ rate concern report.

text.p: The key March three-month Euroyen contract ended the day session on Friday weaker after failing to recover all losses incurred by a local news agency report that quoted the Bank of Japan (BOJ) as saying that it is concerned about excessive falls in long-term interest rates.
Jiji news agency reported on Friday that the BOJ is concerned about any excessive decline in long-term interest rates. The BOJ said it would not comment on the report.

A senior BOJ official was quoted as saying that recent moves in Japan's long-term interest rates run counter to the firm trend in share prices, which is reflecting the BOJ's view that the economy is recovering gradually, Jiji said.
March tumbled to a low of 99.15 immediately after the report, falling through a five-day moving average of 99.18 at which many had expected there was some support.

However, a further fall was avoided due to a lack of comments confirming the report from the BOJ, and traders' wariness to boost fresh positions ahead of the end-September interim corporate book closings.
"A massive 5,000 contracts worth of sell orders were sprung by the report, however, the panic was short-lived due to the lack of follow-through selling," said an European bank trader.
The benchmark three-month certificate of deposit (CD) was traded at 0.53 percent with 10 billion yen turnover. It has been standing at 0.53 since September 3.
The overnight call rate was most actively traded at 0.48 percent, down from 0.49 percent on Thursday.
The Bank of Japan conducted an operation that was neutral to the market and fully offset the estimated shortfall of 400 billion yen.

Despite the market declines on Friday, swap traders who had losses with interest rate swap payments in recent months have reversed their positions and were on the receiving side, suggesting their conviction was that rates will not rise in the near future.
Traders said the dissolution of parliament's Lower House on Friday had little impact on the market.
